title: Absolute, relative and percentage error
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:56Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, mat-percentage-error, covers only percentage error and never teaches relative error as its own step, while mat-accuracy-measurements defines absolute error as half the smallest unit, which conflicts with this brief, so no bank point teaches the same three-part idea.

draft.title: Absolute, relative and percentage error
card: Every measurement is an estimate, so it can differ from the actual value. Error describes how far off it is.
Absolute error
the gap between the measured value and the actual value, with no negative sign. It has the same units as the measurement.
Relative error
absolute error ÷ actual value. It has no units, so it shows how big the gap is compared with the size of the thing measured.
Percentage error
relative error × 100. Example: measured 52 cm, actual 50 cm. Absolute error = 2 cm, relative error = 2 ÷ 50 = 0.04, percentage error = 4%.
draft.remember: Gap first, then divide by the actual value, then multiply by 100 for a percentage.

a.q: A scale reads 84 g for an object that actually has a mass of 80 g. What is the relative error?
a.why: The absolute error is 4 g. Relative error = 4 ÷ 80 = 0.05. Dividing by the measured value, 84, gives 0.048, but the actual value is the one to divide by.
a.clue: Divide the gap by the actual value.

b.q: Ava estimates a tree in Perth is 9.5 m tall. Its actual height is 8 m. What is her percentage error?
b.why: The absolute error is 1.5 m. Relative error = 1.5 ÷ 8 = 0.1875, and × 100 gives 18.75%. Dividing by her estimate of 9.5 gives 15.8%, which uses the wrong value.
b.clue: Divide by the actual height, then turn it into a percentage.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: 4 ÷ 80 = 0.05 and 1.5 ÷ 8 × 100 = 18.75%, and the explanations match the card.
